title: Dispatch: runtime-owned deterministic capability ledger (attempt 1)
description:
PARENT SPEC: eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4 (run `bd show eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4` and read the
2026-09-12 DESIGN SESSION note in full before writing code). Authority: ADR 0020
(especially section 3 and its two load-bearing asymmetries),
docs/design/evidence-trust-model.md (the "Subject authority within adjudication
support" section is directly load-bearing here), the CLOSED W13 bead
eshyra-olc5.6 (which owns capability CONTRACT SHAPE - you do not redefine it),
and AGENTS.md. This child delivers DELIVERABLE 2 only. Deliverable 1 (the record-
relationship manifest) is a sibling child and is NOT yours - do not touch
discovery/expansion.ts, rules/fieldProvenance.ts, rules/packLoader.ts,
rules/bundledSrdPack.ts, or scripts/importers/.

WORKTREE: .worktrees/eshyra-xus8 on branch eshyra-xus8 (already created for you, cut from
branch eshyra-o9bd.19.1.4). Run `cd "$(git rev-parse --show-toplevel)"` first and
work only from there. Run `npm ci` in the worktree before verifying.

=== THE DEFECT (verified; reproduce it before you fix it) ===
The only reviewed statement of Eshyra's positively selected deterministic
capabilities and their bindings to record identities lives inside an AUDIT-BUNDLE
SCRIPT that no runtime consumer may import:
  packages/core/scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts
    RuleDeterministicCapabilityContract   (type; DeterministicCapabilityContract
                                           plus inputSchemaOperation, runtimeOwner, evidence)
    RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_CONTRACTS    resolve-check-v1,
                                               resolve-concentration-v1,
                                               resolve-spell-upcast-v1
    RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_BINDINGS     8 rows, rule key -> capability, many-to-many
    RULE_DETERMINISTIC_CAPABILITY_DISPOSITIONS 31 explicit not-positively-selected rows
    requireRuleDeterministicCapabilityContract / validateRuleDeterministicCapabilityContracts
Because runtime cannot reach it, packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts's
capabilities() instead hardcodes `candidate.entry?.record.kind !== 'magic-item'`
plus a direct import of ONE contract constant
(MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY from state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts),
and every other declaration arrives from a TEST FIXTURE table
(packages/core/test/discovery/support/scenario.ts DECLARED_OFFLINE_CAPABILITIES,
reaching the run as DiscoveryScenario.declaredCapabilities).
Verified consequence: all eight W13-bound rule records exist in the shipped pack -
rule:ability-checks, rule:advantage-and-disadvantage, rule:attack-rolls,
rule:modifiers-to-the-roll, rule:proficiency-bonus, rule:saving-throws,
rule:concentration, rule:casting-a-spell-at-a-higher-level - and every one of them
reaches the DM context packet with ZERO capability entries, byte-identical to a
record for which nothing was positively selected. That directly violates the
parent bead's third acceptance criterion. packetMessage.ts already renders the
non-claim correctly ("no capability was positively selected. / This is not a claim
that the record has no mechanics, is irrelevant, or is safe to ignore.") - the
renderer is honest, the DATA is missing.

=== REQUIRED INVARIANT ===
A runtime consumer obtains positively selected capability bindings and their
declared limits from runtime-owned data reachable from @eshyra/core, without
reading an audit-only artifact; and every negative result is a distinguishable
typed disposition, never an empty value.

=== BUILD THIS ===
1. NEW packages/core/src/rules/deterministicCapabilityLedger.ts.
   MOVE - do not copy - the type, the three contracts, the eight bindings, the 31
   dispositions, and the two fail-closed helpers out of
   scripts/create-dnd5e-srd-audit-bundle/ruleDispositions.ts into this module. The
   audit bundle then IMPORTS them from src, reversing the dependency and keeping
   its reporting byte-identical. Keep inputSchemaOperation, runtimeOwner and
   evidence: those are real capability-OWNER facts, not audit decoration. Do not
   change the contract shape defined by rules/deterministicCapabilityContract.ts -
   eshyra-olc5.6 owns it.
   Also register the existing MAGIC_ITEM_OPERATION_READINESS_CAPABILITY
   (state/itemExecutionReadiness.ts, revision derived-magic-item-clauses-v1) in
   the ledger's contract table so the ledger is the single runtime-owned index of
   selected capabilities. Watch the import direction: if state/ importing rules/
   (or the reverse) would create a cycle, keep the contract constant where it
   lives and have the ledger reference it - say which you did and why in your
   notes.
2. LOOKUP IS A DISCRIMINATED UNION, never a bare array:
     export type CapabilityLedgerLookup =
       | { outcome: 'bound'; recordKey; bindings: readonly CapabilityBinding[] }
       | { outcome: 'not-positively-selected'; recordKey; disposition }
       | { outcome: 'no-statement'; recordKey };
   'no-statement' means the ledger makes NO statement about this record. Document
   in the module doc comment, in ADR 0020 section 3's own terms, that it is a
   statement about Eshyra and never about the rules: it does not mean the record
   has no mechanics, is irrelevant, is safely unsupported, or that the pack is
   complete. A binding QUOTES its contract's identity, revision, required inputs,
   exclusions and residual DM interpretation - it never restates them in its own
   words (packet.ts already follows this quoting discipline; match it).
3. FAIL CLOSED. requireDeterministicCapabilityContract(revision) THROWS on an
   unrecognized revision. Ledger construction validates that every binding names a
   registered contract and that no record key appears in both the binding list and
   the disposition list; either is a construction-time throw. No lookup path may
   return an empty success for an input it could not resolve.
4. CONSUME IT IN DISCOVERY. packages/core/src/discovery/packet.ts's capabilities()
   consults the ledger by record key instead of branching on
   `record.kind !== 'magic-item'`:
   - magic-item candidates carrying capability-preflight routes keep the EXISTING
     real preflight path unchanged (preflightOperation, available/blocked). Do not
     touch its semantics.
   - a candidate whose record key is 'bound' gets one CapabilityPreflight per
     binding with status 'not-evaluated-offline', quoting the contract's
     capabilityId, revision, inputs, exclusions and residualInterpretation. This
     is EXACTLY what the evidence trust model permits for a declaration without
     the owner's subject-specific preflight: "a capability declaration qualifies
     its identity/revision and its declared inputs, exclusions, and residual
     interpretation... it does NOT qualify availability for a candidate,
     operation, or input." Do not invent an 'available' status for these.
   - a candidate whose record key is 'not-positively-selected' must carry that
     explicit disposition - its reason, replacingResponsibility and nextState -
     into the packet rather than silence. Choose the smallest honest
     representation (a new optional field on PacketCandidate is acceptable; a
     fake CapabilityPreflight status is not) and render it in
     discovery/packetMessage.ts under the existing "### Deterministic capability"
     heading, stated as a statement about Eshyra and not about the rules. Keep the
     existing positivelySelected logic correct: a disposition is NOT a positive
     selection.
   - the scenario-injected declaredCapabilities path stays for harness use, but
     must not silently shadow a real ledger binding. If both exist for one
     candidate, prefer the ledger and say so in a comment.
5. EXPORT SURFACE. New core symbols default to @eshyra/core/internal
   (packages/core/src/internal.ts) per AGENTS.md; promote to the root export only
   if a real consumer outside this repo needs it. State your choice in your notes.

=== REGRESSION PREDICATE (assert IDENTITIES, never counts) ===
R1 Each of the eight bound rule keys, BY IDENTITY, yields {outcome:'bound'} with
   its exact expected capability revision (rule:concentration ->
   resolve-concentration-v1; rule:casting-a-spell-at-a-higher-level ->
   resolve-spell-upcast-v1; the other six -> resolve-check-v1).
R2 rule:attunement (a disposition row) yields 'not-positively-selected' carrying
   its reason. A record in neither list (pick a real pack key, e.g. a creature)
   yields 'no-statement'. All three outcomes are distinguishable at the type level.
R3 THE DISCRIMINATING PACKET CONTROL: build a context packet containing
   rule:concentration and assert it carries a declared capability entry naming
   resolve-concentration-v1 with the contract's exclusions and residual
   interpretation. The current code produces an empty set here - the test must
   fail against the pre-fix behaviour.
R4 requireDeterministicCapabilityContract('not-a-real-revision') throws. A ledger
   built with a binding naming an unregistered contract throws at construction. A
   record key present in both bindings and dispositions throws at construction.
R5 No capability entry is produced for any record merely because it carries typed
   mechanics or executionReadiness clauses (W13's "no capability may be inferred
   from the presence of typed fields"). Pin this with a record that has typed
   mechanics and no binding.
R6 The magic-item available/blocked preflight results are unchanged: pin at least
   one available and one blocked identity from the existing tests.
R7 The audit bundle's reported capability rows are identical after the move -
   same identities, same order-independent membership. Keep
   packages/core/test/ruleDispositions.test.ts passing, adjusting only import
   paths; do not weaken an assertion.

=== VERIFICATION ===
npm run verify:worktree BEFORE committing (it rewrites files). If the audit-bundle
move changes any generated audit output, run the audit-bundle script and explain
every diff in your completion notes; an unexplained diff is a stop-and-report.

=== PROHIBITIONS ===
No corpus-wide capability inventory and no completeness claim. No uniform
execution-readiness disposition for every clause. No widening of engine:F1-F10
beyond the generated magic-item backlog, and no readiness or engine-hook count
reported as a capability inventory. No change to the W13 contract shape. No new
capability invented to make a record look covered. Absence of a binding is a
statement about Eshyra, never about the rules. Do not weaken an existing test or
audit expectation to make this pass.

If the work reveals a new root cause or requires churn outside the direct
consequences of this minimal change, stop and report instead of broadening it.
